authority: User $implement request; approved CW-15/C-D52; fresh lost-intent handoff review
objective: Prevent a successful handoff reopen from erasing a newer concurrent takeover request, preserving all established submission-claim and no-replay behavior.
required_changes: Make every takeover intent set advance a monotonic fence generation. Handoff captures the generation it is returning and may reopen only if that exact generation is still current; a newer request makes reopen a no-op and stays revoked.

A successful conditional reopen must advance generation again so all older lifecycle permits remain invalid. Failure to reopen because of a newer request is not a handoff failure: durable manager control may exist, but automatic admission remains closed until that new takeover request is processed and later handed off.

Add a deterministic three-thread regression: handoff durably commits manager control, newer request sets intent before conditional reopen, automatic dispatch races, and both command/review remain zero after the newer invocation. Then allow the new request to acquire the lifecycle lock and prove its durable state is not lost.

Retain normal same-coordinator handoff reopening, external/commit failure closure, revoke-before-claim/claim-before-revoke semantics, exact epoch invalidation and token-negative behavior. Do not change the approved claim-as-submission linearization interpretation.
constraints: Surgical generation-aware correction only. No other production/docs/workflow/PLAN/state, G3 protocol changes, external OMP/reboot, delegation, dependency installation, commit, publish, deploy or Docker. Use apply_patch; focused RED/GREEN and full non-live regressions, graphify/hash/residue.
report: Return candidate_ready/needs_reroute; exact generation values/thread order/action counts/durable states; normal/failure handoff and submission-claim regressions; hashes/suites/residue/pending.
